A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same VSRM work, with matching scientific text, equations, tables and figures. Neither contains an appendix; both mention a separate supplementary file that is not supplied. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VSRM benchmark results, ablations, qualitative comparisons and complexity measurements in Section 5, Tables 2–8 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original VSRM experimental results, including benchmark PSNR/SSIM scores and component ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same VSRM architecture, spatial/temporal Mamba blocks, temporal gated feed-forward network, deformable cross-Mamba alignment and combined spatial/frequency losses.

E1.justification: Both use REDS and Vimeo-90K for training and REDS4, Vimeo-90K-T and Vid4 for evaluation of ×4 video super-resolution. No evaluated dataset, task or scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains EDVR, VSR-T, VRT, BasicVSR++, RVRT, PSRT-recurrent and IART in the same comparisons. Comparator membership in the ablations, visual comparisons and complexity analysis also remains unchanged; only citation numbers change.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 2 retain the same REDS4 holdout clips, bicubic degradation, ×4 scale, PSNR/SSIM metrics and input-frame configurations. No stated ablation or runtime evaluation setting changes.

E4.justification: Tables 3–7 retain the same backbone, alignment, scan-direction, feed-forward-network and frequency-loss ablations. Figures 5–6 retain the same qualitative examples and effective receptive-field analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 2–8 and qualitative findings in Figures 5–6 match. For example, Table 2 retains VSRM's REDS4 result of 33.11 dB PSNR and 0.9162 SSIM with 16 input frames.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same state-space definitions, discretization, module equations, Fourier formulation and loss definitions in Equations 1–15. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about first adapting Mamba to VSR, introducing the proposed blocks, alignment and frequency loss, and achieving state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of receptive-field benefits, alignment flexibility, frequency-loss behavior and performance/complexity trade-offs are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The disclosed loss weights, pretrained SpyNet usage and RTX A6000 48GB runtime hardware remain unchanged. Both defer the same details to a separate supplement; no implementation or code/data-access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds bibliography entries [51], Trans2UNet: neural fusion for nuclei semantic segmentation, and [52], Channel-partitioned windowed attention and frequency learning for single image super-resolution. Neither is cited or discussed in the body. All previous references and substantive research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Citation numbers are updated following the bibliography additions, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional references reflow the final bibliography page, moving the end of the Vision Mamba reference into the right column. All figures and tables retain their arrangement, formatting and captions apart from citation numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds two bibliography entries without integrating them into the discussion, alongside citation and layout updates. The method, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
